items.title: MCX Q2 profit jumps over two-fold to ₹455 crore as trading volumes surge
points: Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) has reported a more than two-fold jump in consolidated net profit to Rs 455 crore for the September quarter of FY27, driven by a sharp rise in income and trading volumes.
The bourse had posted a net profit of Rs 197.47 crore in the year-ago period, according to a regulatory filing.
Total income surged to Rs 799.66 crore from Rs 374.23 crore a year earlier.
Expenses rose to Rs 211.36 crore from Rs 150.41 crore.
On the volume front, the Average Daily Turnover (ADT) of futures climbed to Rs 62,819 crore during the quarter, while that of options rose to Rs 12,00,129 crore.
The exchange also saw physical deliveries of 5.68 tonnes of gold, 199.91 tonnes of silver and 34,707 tonnes of base metals during the quarter.

"Our strong performance in Q2 FY27 reflects the continued trust of market participants and the growing relevance of the exchange in the evolving commodity ecosystem," said Praveena Rai, MD and CEO, MCX.

items.title: Delhi Police files FIR against Prashant Bhushan for allegedly sharing doctored video of Russian FM criticising India
points: The Delhi Police on Tuesday registered a First Information Report (FIR) against senior Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan for sharing a digitally manipulated video of Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, which purportedly contained remarks hostile to…
The FIR was lodged at the Special Cell police station after police, during cyber patrolling on November 3, came across a social media post by the handle @thequotesnews.
The post claimed that a doctored video of Lavrov had been shared from Bhushan's X account.

“On 03.11.2026, during cyber patrolling, it came to notice that the social media handle @thequotesnews has claimed that a purported doctored video of the Russian Foreign Minister, hostile to India, was shared from Prashant Bhushan's handle @pbhushan1,”…
In this regard, a case under Section 336(4)/353(1)(c)/356/340(2) BNS and 66C IT Act has been registered as FIR No. 263/26 at PS Special Cell,” it added.
The FIR comes after the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) debunked the digitally manipulated video falsely attributed to Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov.

items.title: TDP-led alliance sweeps Andhra Pradesh civic elections; YSRCP alleges manipulation
points: Andhra Pradesh’s ruling Telugu Desam Party (TDP)-led alliance won seven of the 13 municipal corporations and was leading in another five in the early hours of Wednesday.
It bagged 75 out of 86 municipalities and nagar panchayats.
The ruling alliance’s chairpersons were elected uncontested across 17 municipalities and nagar panchayats.
The Opposition Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party (YSRCP), which won all 13 municipal corporations in 2021, appeared set to win one (Anantapur municipal corporation).
In Pulivendula municipality of the district, Reddy’s home constituency, TDP’s chairperson candidate Tugutla Geetha Kumari won by a margin of 13,875 votes.
TDP fielded 13 mayoral candidates, Jana Sena Party two, and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) one.
For the remaining 70 posts, the TDP fielded 49 candidates, the Jana Sena 17 and the BJP four.
Srinivasa Rao is Senior Assistant Editor based out of Hyderabad covering developments in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana .

items.title: China Boosts Market Defense With National Team Buying, Buybacks
points: China escalated its defense of the stock market, as state-backed funds answered the government’s rallying call by increasing purchases and more companies stepped up buyback plans.
A basket of nine exchange-traded funds that are favored by the so-called national team of investors drew 76.7 billion yuan of inflows on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg-compiled data.
That was the second largest on record and most since April 8, 2025, when markets were then hammered by President Donald Trump’s tariff announcement.
China’s tech-heavy Star 50 Index stabilized on Wednesday after tumbling nearly 4% in the previous session.
“The latest developments in the market point to Beijing’s growing recognition that more support is needed,” said Homin Lee, senior macro strategist at Lombard Odier in Singapore.

items.title: Centre asks OTT platforms, news sites to time-stamp visuals and follow IT law 'in letter and spirit'
points: The Union information and broadcasting ministry on Monday issued an advisory to OTT platforms, digital news publishers, and intermediaries, seeking “strict adherence” to the Information Technology Act, 2000, and its rules, after noting instances of…

“All the OTT Platforms and the Digital News Publishers are hereby advised to ensure strict adherence to the statutory provisions governing content published on online platforms, in letter and spirit,” the advisory said.
In an advisory dated October 21, it covered AI use in programme production, crime reporting, disturbing visuals, live coverage of security operations, studio debates and maps.
It asked channels to time-stamp visuals wherever necessary.
In brief, publishers are asked to time-stamp visuals with the original date, location and context, and to name outside sources, including social media.
Disaster visuals should be date-stamped, and only Survey of India maps should be used.
Intermediaries are separately told to meet their Section 79 duties, with “particular attention” to Rules 3(3) and 4(1A) on synthetically generated information.

items.title: No respite for Delhiites as pollution levels surge; AQI at 373, 21 stations in ‘severe’ category
points: Delhi’s pollution levels continued to surge on Wednesday morning, with 21 of the 59 monitoring stations recording air quality in the ‘severe’ category.
The Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 373 at 7:05 am, in the ‘very poor’ category, compared with Tuesday’s 24-hour average of 350.
At 54 of the 59 monitoring stations, PM2.5 was the primary pollutant.
Punjabi Bagh recorded the highest AQI at 452, followed by Jahangirpuri (450) and IIT Delhi (446).
Five stations were in the ‘poor’ category and the remaining 23 in the very poor category.
The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) classifies an AQI of 0-50 as ‘good’, 51-100 as ‘satisfactory’, 101-200 as ‘moderate’, 201-300 as ‘poor’, 301-400 as ‘very poor’ and 401-500 as ‘severe’.
According to the Air Quality Early Warning System (AQEWS), air quality is expected to remain in the very poor category from November 4 to 6.
NASA satellite data detected 1,561 farm fires in Punjab and Haryana between October 1 and November 3 - 1,406 in Punjab and 155 in Haryana.

items.title: JNU to confer ‘Professor Emeritus’ title on Amitabh Mattoo
points: Amitabh Mattoo, Dean School of International Studies (SIS), JNU.
Credit: X/@amitabhmattoo The Executive Council of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) has decided to confer the title ‘Professor Emeritus’ on Amitabh Mattoo, Dean School of International Studies (SIS).
Mr. Mattoo’s name was recommended by Rajesh Rajagopalan professor from SIS.
After deliberations at the meeting, it was decided that title of ‘Professor Emeritus’ in JNU would be conferred effective after the date of his voluntary retirement on February 28, 2027.
Before being made Dean in 2024, Mr. Mattoo was Chair of the Centre for International Politics, Organisation and Disarmament at SIS.
Also a former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jammu, he is the only Padma Shri awardee currently on the rolls of JNU.
Speaking to The Hindu, Mr. Mattoo said that JNU has never been simply a place where he works but has been his intellectual home and the crucible of his ideas.

items.title: Airport charges account for only 5-6% of airfares: GMR executive
points: Airport charges account for only 5-6% of airfares and are linked to the investment needed to expand infrastructure, a senior GMR executive said while defending the rising cost of airport operations.
The development came a day after IndiGo chief executive officer (CEO) Willie Walsh had called for lower airport charges and taxes.
“Airport charges are too high and so this market would do much better if we had lower taxes.
So lower taxes, lower airport charges, that is the way forward,” Walsh said on Monday, arguing that airports should be more competitive in their pricing as they are effective monopolies.
Offering a contrasting view, SGK Kishore, executive director of GMR Group, said airport charges were not determined arbitrarily by airport operators but through a regulated process.
“There is a clear economic regulator (Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act) who looks into what the airport charges should be.

items.title: Truck driver runs over police inspector in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas, arrested after brief encounter
points: Police on Tuesday arrested a truck driver who had allegedly run over and killed the Khategaon police station in-charge in Madhya Pradesh's Dewas.
The accused, identified as Gajendra alias Akku Rawat, had allegedly run over inspector Dilip Puri during a search for illicit liquor on the Indore-Betul highway on Sunday.
A reward of ₹10,000 had been announced for his arrest.
When the police were bringing him back to Dewas, the accused tried to escape, but the cops arrested him after a brief encounter.
“The encounter took place within the jurisdiction of Barotha police station near Dewas when the arrested accused attempted to escape from police custody.
Gajendra, a resident of Alirajpur, was the driver of the Eicher truck (MP-43-H-4786) which was allegedly being used to smuggle illicit liquor.
Police have already arrested three persons, including the kingpin, Rahul Jaiswal of Timarni; his accomplice, Vijay Rao; and Keram Singh Changod of Alirajpur, who had provided the vehicle to Gajendra.

items.title: Armed man holds receptionist hostage during robbery bid in bag repair shop at Indiranagar in Bengaluru
points: The incident took a dramatic turn when the woman managed to free her hands and raise an alarm, attracting the attention of passers-by.
In a filmy scene, the accused then held her hostage at knifepoint and threatened the people who began gathering outside, triggering panic in the busy locality.
Claiming that someone was trying to kill him, the man suddenly jumped over the counter in a bid to get close to the receptionist.
When the woman attempted to call the shopowner, the accused allegedly forced her to sit down, held her mouth shut, and threatened to kill her if she screamed.
He then allegedly attacked her with a knife, applied gum to her hands, and stuck them to the desk.
He stuffed a piece of cloth in her mouth before forcibly removing her gold mangalsutra weighing around 35 grams.
When passers-by rushed inside the shop, the accused grabbed the woman by the hair, dragged her to a side, and held a knife to her neck.

items.title: Ex-DTU student among 3 held for duping people, promising admissions: Police
points: A former Delhi Technological University (DTU) student, who allegedly posed as a university staff member to cheat families by promising admissions, is among the three people arrested for running a fake admission racket, police said on Wednesday.
The main accused, Yashraj Bajpai, allegedly lured prospective students and their families by claiming he could secure admission to DTU.
The complainant, Dr Kritika Joshi, approached Shahbad Dairy police after allegedly being cheated of around ₹8.5 lakh on the pretext of arranging admission for her daughter.
The other two accused, identified as Sonu alias Yuvraj, 32, and Devender Singh, 30, were arrested from Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh on October 26.
Both were absconding and traced through technical surveillance, police said.
A first information report (FIR) was registered at Shahbad Dairy police station under sections 318(4), 336, 338(3), 340(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
